newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL ANNOUNCE 'INTEREST' IN BUYING RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL ANNOUNCE 'INTEREST' IN BUYING RONALDO.

text.p: Real Madrid president Lorenzo Sanz said on Thursday his club were considering signing star striker Ronaldo from arch-rivals Barcelona.
"If Inter don't go ahead, we're interested," said Sanz.
Inter Milan became hot favourites to buy the Brazilian after negotiations between the players' agents and Barcelona broke down two weeks ago.
Sanz made his comments after meeting Giovanni Branchini, who manages Ronaldo and Real striker Davor Suker.

Earlier this week Sanz withdrew an offer to serve as intermediary for Inter after FIFA ruled that the Italian side cannot buy Ronaldo by paying the 4.5 billion peseta ($30.9 million) 'withdrawal clause' stipulated in his contract, as a Spanish club would.
As a result Inter appear to have no option but to negotiate with Barcelona.
Press speculation suggests the price asked for the striker could be eight billion pesetas (($55.2 million).
FIFA Secretary-General Joseph Blatter has confirmed that Barcelona have the right to charge formation fees for Ronaldo in any transfer.
The repercussions of the Ronaldo case could be immense.
The matter has drawn the attention of Jean Louis Dupont, the lawyer who won the case for Belgian player Marc Bosman obliging European Union clubs to scrap quotas for EU players.
The Spanish Football Federation has promised to defend Barcelona's case, while the players' union could take up Ronaldo's side.

"If Ronaldo asks, the Association will defend him, because we believe he is right," said Gerardo Movilla Gonzalez of the Association of Spanish Footballers in comments published by the Spanish press on Thursday.
In another development, Barcelona president Jose Luis Nunez threatened on Thursday to report Real to FIFA for 'poaching' Sampdoria midfielder Christian Karembeu.
Barcelona agreed terms with Sampdoria earlier this season, but the French international refused to move, saying he had already reached agreement with Real Madrid.
"Barcelona negotiated with Sampdoria, legally. Real Madrid negotiated with a player under contract with another club ... illegally," said Nunez.
The conflict over the transfer has been stirred up in recent days by Real's intervention in the Ronaldo case.
Sanz has said publicly that he would like to even the score with Barcelona for the Karembeu incident.
